props.title: Detective Conan: Strategy Above the Depths
props.initialSlug: Conan races to stop a bomber targeting a luxury liner

sections.content: Detective Conan: Strategy Above the Depths (2005) represents a pinnacle in the Detective Conan film series, bringing Shinichi Kudo's sleuthing to a maritime setting. The film builds on the franchise's signature blend of intricate mysteries and action sequences established in Case Closed: The Time Bombed Skyscraper (1997). Like The Last Wizard of the Century (1999), it maintains the delicate balance between complex deduction and accessible entertainment that made Detective Conan a phenomenon in Japanese animation.

sections.content: Strategy Above the Depths particularly excels in its confined-space tension, reminiscent of classics like Speed (1994) and Under Siege (1992). The maritime setting on the Pacific Serenade cruise ship creates a pressure-cooker atmosphere where Conan must solve the mystery before the ship becomes a massive weapon. The film's technical accuracy regarding naval operations and maritime law shows influence from sophisticated thrillers like The Hunt for Red October (1990).

The film's handling of multiple concurrent threats - the immediate danger to passengers, the larger terrorist plot, and the interpersonal dynamics between suspects - demonstrates the mature storytelling that elevated Detective Conan beyond typical animated mysteries. This complexity recalls the layered narratives of Perfect Blue (1997) and Ghost in the Shell (1995), other landmark Japanese animated films that refused to underestimate their audience. sections.content: Strategy Above the Depths marked a significant evolution in how Detective Conan handled large-scale threats while maintaining intimate character moments. The film's influence can be seen in later maritime anime mysteries like One Piece Film: Gold (2016) and Black Butler: Book of the Atlantic (2017). The technical detail in depicting ship operations raised the bar for accuracy in animated detective stories.
